text:
Alex (sales): FYI FinEdge wants final numbers for an enterprise commit — 2000 qps bursty chat + embeddings at peak. They asked about reserved GPUs, autoscale behavior, and the security questionnaire.
Maya (solutions): Quick q: is 2000 qps steady or 2000 peak with 50 rps baseline? their doc says 'bursty day-of-week spikes'.
FinEdge PM: Mostly peak. baseline ~100 rps, spikes to ~2k for 10-15m windows, maybe twice/day. KV cache should help for repeated prompts.
Jon (eng-infra): Ok. For reserved capacity we can map that to a Dedicated pool. Rough calc: 2k qps chat with 32-token avg -> ~64k tokens/s. With our Llama-8B quantized perf profile that’s ~6 responses/sec/GPU? Wait let me put numbers: one p4d-like instance (8xA100 equiv) supports ~350 qps for typical chat. So 6-7 of those = ~2450 qps headroom. That suggests 7 reserved nodes + autoscale.
Maya (solutions): Can we present an option with smaller reservation + burst credits/autoscale? Sales needs pricing delta.
Jon (eng-infra): Yes. Option A: reserve 7 nodes (peak covered, predictable unit cost). Option B: reserve 3 nodes + autoscale pool for bursts (cheaper base, potential prewarm latency). Option C: reserve 0 + full autoscale (cheapest up-front but not SLA for tail latency).
Sam (sre): Important: autoscale coldstart can add 2-30s tail latency depending on model init and KV warmup. We mitigate with prewarm hooks and KV warmup shim.
Alex (sales): FinEdge asked if KV warmup can be guaranteed during spikes. What’s realistic?
Jon (eng-infra): We can run proactive KV warming for commonly used prefixes. Kubernetes prewarm job + synthetic replay will prime KV. Not instantaneous: warming 10M tokens into KV takes time and IOPS; but for repeated queries it reduces generation cost and latency after warmup. For the twice/day 15m spikes we can schedule a prewarm 5m before expected spike (customer schedule needed).
Maya (solutions): Can you paste a sample autoscale policy and an example prewarm command we can include in the handoff doc?
Jon (eng-infra): Sure — snippet below (ops-ready, abbreviated):
```
autoscale_policy: {
  min_replicas: 3,
  target_rps_per_replica: 100,
  cooldown_sec: 60,
  max_replicas: 10,
  prewarm_hook: '/ops/prewarm --model=llama-8b-q --tokens=500k --prefixes=top100'
}
```
Prewarm command (one-off):
```
./prewarm --model llama-8b-q --prefix-file common_prefixes.txt --parallel 8 --duration 300
```
Sam (sre): Also add health-check: if startup fails 3x -> fallback to quantized-4bit variant in region to avoid total outage.
Alex (sales): Pricing side — how do we show the math? FinEdge needs monthly committed cost vs burst credit burn rate.
Maya (solutions): Example calculation: reserve 7 nodes X $X/node/mo = committed cost. For option B: reserve 3 nodes + burst pool charged at usage-per-token for extra replicas spun up. We should give a sample month with 60 spike events to show expected burst burn.
Jon (eng-infra): I'll run a quick sim and return numbers. For now: assume one extra node costs ~0.12$/min equivalent. A 15m spike with +4 nodes -> ~7.2$ per spike -> 60 spikes => ~432$/mo burst burn plus base reserved cost.
FinEdge PM: That per-spike figure helps. Do you have a playbook for 'warm vs cold' decision making? customer wants to avoid degraded UX.
Sam (sre): Playbook (short):
- If spikes are predictable (schedule): prewarm 5–10m before.
- If spikes unpredictable but frequent: reserve more base capacity.
- If unpredictable & rare: use autoscale + low-latency fallback model (quantized variant) + notify.
Maya (solutions): Security / questionnaire — they attached the infosec PDF. Rachel, can you confirm Dedicated meets their encryption/KMS asks? They want per-tenant KMS and audit logs.
Rachel (security): Dedicated + Private both support customer KMS (via our KMS integration) and VPC peering. Audit logs available for 90 days on standard plan; enterprise retention is an add-on. I’ll flag three items they listed: SOC2 controls mapping, KMS key rotation cadence, and network egress rules. I'll fill those in the questionnaire by EOD.
Alex (sales): Perfect. Any enterprise blockers we should call out to FinEdge now? e.g., software license, data residency, billing terms.
Maya (solutions): For commit sizing blockers: need a signed expected traffic profile (time windows + QPS distribution) and whether they require AZ spread for resilience. Also we need approval on fallback model acceptance (some customers want strict output parity; quantized fallback may change outputs slightly).
FinEdge PM: We can provide traffic logs and we prefer AZ spread. Fallback model needs to be listed in contract as 'compatible variant' — ok to test.
Jon (eng-infra): Action items: (1) I’ll run a perf sim with their sample trace and produce three pricing options; (2) Sam will draft prewarm/fallback runbook; (3) Rachel will answer security questionnaire items; (4) Maya/Alex to confirm contract language for fallback models and AZ spread.
Sam (sre): I'll post the runbook snippet here when done. TL;DR: for high SLA choose reserve >=70% of expected peak and autoscale remainder.
Alex (sales): Thanks team. Maya — can you create the customer-facing slide with Option A/B/C numbers? Need it for Friday call.
Maya (solutions): On it. I'll include the sim numbers once Jon posts them.
deploy-bot: Deploy completed: perf-sim-job-1708765460 finished (status: success)
Jon (eng-infra): Perf sim results uploaded: summary -> Option A (7 reserved): $XX,XXX/mo, median latency 120ms, p99 420ms. Option B (3 reserved+autoscale): $YY,YYY/mo + ~$432/mo burst in sample month, median 140ms, p99 650ms. Option C (autoscale-only): $ZZ,ZZZ/mo, median 180ms, p99 1.8s. Full CSV attached in shared drive.
Alex (sales): This is golden. I'll draft the pricing email and attach the security answers. Closing loop once Rachel's questionnaire is in.
Rachel (security): Questionnaire answers posted to shared drive + annotated comments. Noted: need contractual guarantee for KMS usage and expanded log retention (we'll add as add-on in SOW).
FinEdge PM: Thanks all — we'll review and come back with signed schedule after internal review. Appreciate the clear options.
Maya (solutions): Marking as blocked->waiting_on_customer until we get signed schedule + traffic trace.
